items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: You know two little kids that stayed with me, Oliver Jackson and Eddie Locke. I used to tell them, "You're going to play with Earl Hines -"

ctx.x: We had that. When you was in this category you played into this club. You did not go over here and play into this club until you qualified, then you begin to move up and you sit in over here. Then as I said, the older guys when they got ready to semi-retire, they went and got a young man and set him down in the home and gave him the book and they went to the bandleader and said, "He's taking my place." But they don't have that now because

we've had a hectic situation for 22 years. But we could never know, with all this wealth of talent out here - and we're not in a position, we don't travel around even though we got the airplane and everything - we're not in a position because we're not set in our views. We've gone into certain things. Like I'm with a drum shop for 2 years and my heart bleeds that I can't go out and give this.
